newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Bradesco, Itau to bid on Banerj selloff.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Bradesco, Itau to bid on Banerj selloff.

text.p: Brazilian private banks Bradesco and Banco Itau will be the only bidders on Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj sell-off on Tuesday, officials said.

The other six prequalified investors -- Banco BBA Creditanstalt, Bank of Boston Brazil unit, General Electric Co's General Electric Capital Corporation, Banco CCF do Brasil, Companhia de Investimentos Latino-Americana and Golden Cross -- have dropped out of the running.
Although only two investors will participate in the auction, Rio de Janeiro state government is confident that the bank will be sold off.
"I have no doubts that Banerj will be privatized," said Henrique Dittmar, executive secretary of Rio de Janeiro state's privatization program committee.
Even possible court injunctions asking for the suspension of the auction are not seen as a concern.
"We knew that it could happen," said Dittmar, referring to action from Banerj's pension fund and an association of Banerj's minority shareholders against the sell-off.
So far the state court has not made any decision.
Banerj's selloff is part of Rio de Janeiro's 9.0 billion real debt restructuring package being negotiated with the federal government.

With 193 branches, Banerj bank has a net worth of 180 million reais and total assets of 4.0 billion reais. Under Bozano's management, Banerj's staff was cut to 8,226 employees from 11,970 workers in December 1995.
Dittmar said the two remaining bidders have considered Banerj under their strategy to consolidate their position in Rio de Janeiro.
Banerj, the first Brazilian state bank to be privatized, has been administered by private bank Bozano, Simonsen, hired to ready the bank for privatization.

Banerj and its insurance firm Banerj Seguros will be auctioned off for a minimum price of 436.693 million reais and 43.310 million reais, respectively, at a closed-envelope auction on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange (BVRJ).
Investors will have to acquire the bank and its insurer together, which means that bids totalling less than 480 million reais will not be accepted.

The bidders will be allowed to pay off 30 million reais -- 27 million reais of Banerj's base price and 3.0 million reais of the insurer's base price -- in Privatization Certificates, which represent state securitized debt.

Banerj's tender details also noted that the World Bank's International Finance Corp (IFC) has shown interest in taking part in the privatization by offering loans to the new majority shareholder or by acquiring a stake in Banerj later.

Bozano was awarded a contract last January to run Banerj, replacing the Central Bank which had taken over Banerj in December 1994. The bank has received 36 million reais for the job and will be paid five percent of the auction's receipts.
Cash deposits at the bank rose to 428.6 million reais from 306.7 million reais late last year, while time deposits grew to 1.246 billion reais from 487.7 million reais in the same period.
